title: Rheingau
description: A south-facing slope along the Rhine where Spätlese was born and Riesling grew noble.
L: The Rheingau lies where the Rhine, blocked by the Taunus hills, turns west for about 30 km between Wiesbaden and Rüdesheim. Vineyards face south across the wide river, catching full sun. The Taunus shelters them from cold northern winds. It's small, about 3,200 hectares. Assmannshausen and Lorch extend it north-west.

The Rheingau is warmer than the Mosel. The wide Rhine, nearly a kilometre across, reflects light and moderates temperature; the Taunus blocks cold air. Soils vary: slate and quartzite on higher slopes, like Rüdesheim's Berg; loess and marl lower down. Wines are fuller and riper than the Mosel's, often dry.
What shelters the Rheingau from cold northern winds?

Cistercian monks founded Kloster Eberbach in 1136 and planted the Steinberg, a walled vineyard like Burgundy's clos. Schloss Johannisberg, on a hill above the Rhine, was a Benedictine abbey. Noble families and monasteries owned most land for centuries, so the Rheingau has many large historic estates.
Kloster Eberbach was founded by Cistercian monks.
The Rheingau faces south where the Rhine turns west
It's warmer than the Mosel, giving fuller wines
Monasteries like Kloster Eberbach shaped its history

Riesling covers about 78% of the Rheingau, the highest share of any German region. It gives fuller, riper wines than the Mosel's, with peach, apricot, citrus and spice, firm acidity and often more alcohol. Most top Rheingau Riesling today is dry.

Spätburgunder, Pinot Noir, covers about 12%, mostly in Assmannshausen, on red slate, famous for red wine since the Middle Ages. The wines are elegant, with red cherry and spice. Assmannshäuser Höllenberg is the most famous red vineyard.
Match each term to the Rheingau.
The Rheingau is Riesling with a red exception.
Rheingau Riesling is often described as a little more serious and structured than Mosel Riesling, with more body and spice.
What share of the Rheingau's vineyards is Riesling?
Riesling covers about 78%, fuller than the Mosel's

Explain the role of noble rot

In 1775, the monks of Schloss Johannisberg needed permission from the Prince-Bishop of Fulda to start the harvest. The messenger returned weeks late. By then, the grapes had shrivelled with noble rot. The monks made wine anyway, and it was remarkable. That late harvest, Spätlese, became a recognised style.

The story shows the role of Botrytis cinerea: when grapes are left on the vine in misty autumn weather, noble rot concentrates sugar and acidity and adds honeyed aromas. From Spätlese came Auslese, selected bunches, and later Beerenauslese and Trockenbeerenauslese, picked berry by berry.
Why was the 1775 harvest at Schloss Johannisberg late?
The messenger with permission arrived weeks late
The delay let noble rot develop, creating Spätlese.

Schloss Johannisberg sits on a hill above the Rhine, on the 50th parallel, with vineyards on a steep slope. It's one of the first estates planted entirely with Riesling, from 1720. A statue of the messenger, the Spätlesereiter, stands in its courtyard. Its wines use coloured capsules to mark quality levels.
Which developed from the Spätlese tradition?
Spätlese was born at Schloss Johannisberg in 1775
Noble rot concentrated the late-picked grapes
Schloss Johannisberg was planted entirely with Riesling from 1720

The VDP, Verband Deutscher Prädikatsweingüter, is an association of about 200 top German estates, founded in 1910. Its emblem is an eagle with grapes on the bottle capsule. The Rheingau's Charta association, from 1984, pioneered dry, food-friendly Riesling and site classification, ideas the VDP adopted nationally.

The VDP's pyramid, like Burgundy's, has four levels: Gutswein, estate wine; Ortswein, village wine; Erste Lage, first-class site; and Grosse Lage, great site. Dry wines from Grosse Lage sites are called Grosses Gewächs, GG. Sweet wines from top sites still use Prädikat terms, like Spätlese or Auslese.
Order the VDP levels from broadest to most precise.
Each step narrows the origin and raises the standard.

German wine law ranks wine by grape ripeness, not by site. The VDP's private classification brings site to the centre, as in Burgundy. Rheingau sites like Rüdesheimer Berg Schlossberg, Erbacher Marcobrunn and Hochheimer Hölle are Grosse Lage. Not all great producers are VDP members.
A dry wine from a Grosse Lage site
GG marks the VDP's top dry wines.
The VDP is an association of about 200 top estates
Its pyramid runs from Gutswein to Grosse Lage
Grosses Gewächs is a dry wine from a top site
Reading the Rheingau and eating with it

Labels show producer, village plus vineyard, like Rüdesheimer Berg Rottland, the grape, the Prädikat or trocken, and the VDP eagle if a member. GG means dry top-site wine. Erstes Gewächs was the Rheingau's older term for top dry wines. Spätburgunder from Assmannshausen is labelled as red.

Dry Rheingau Riesling suits pork, veal, river fish like trout and pike, white asparagus, a German spring favourite, and schnitzel. Off-dry and Spätlese suit spicy food and roast pork. Spätburgunder suits game birds and mushrooms. Serve Riesling at 8 to 11 degrees.
Which German spring vegetable suits dry Rheingau Riesling?
Spargel season is a German ritual.
Good Rheingau GG Riesling ages 10 to 20 years, developing honey, toast and petrol notes while keeping its acidity.
GG wines from the VDP are sweet.
Not true. GG wines are dry.
